texts: On day 16 of Year 1, a cold wind blew off the sea at night.
The cold wind struck the Cliff Path at night.
The cold wind came before the first hard frost.
Keepers on the Cliff Path had not yet added salt-bloom to the mire-essence, because the salt-bloom season had not started.
Eleven lanterns on the Middle Row were unprepared.
The eleven lanterns went out before dawn.
No lantern at the Sunken Cove went out.
No lantern in the Northcove went out.
The cliff-spires sheltered the Northcove against the north wind.

q1_issues.issue: The distributive rule for "Eleven lanterns ... were unprepared" drops the clause's past tense — the conclusion is the bare (Member $x unprepared) where the surface-tense-decides rule for copular clauses requires the Past-wrapped atom.

(Member sk_wind_1 north_wind), together with the (Against sk_shelter_1 sk_wind_1) filler at index 59, identifies the day-16 cold wind that blew off the sea with "the north wind" and asserts it is a north wind, which the text never states.

The bare-plural (indefinite) subject "Keepers on the Cliff Path" has its (GroupOf sk_keepers_1 keeper) and (On sk_keepers_1 cliff_path) atoms outside the strength-0 denial, where the determiner test places an indefinite's witness and typing inside the bundle.

q2_gaps: a solid-spelled name whose kind word is fused into it ("the Northcove") — the type-atom licence covers a kind word sitting inside a multi-word name ("the Kestrel River" → river), but proper nouns are exempt from decomposition, so it is unstated whether Northcove licenses (Member northcove cove) the way "the Sunken Cove" does; the parse emitted the type atom for one and not the other

Ordinal over an event-noun kind ("the first hard frost") — the scale slot is specified as the associated event or an explicit -est dimension, with no guidance when the ranked thing is itself the event-noun class (here the class symbol hard_frost was put in the scale slot)

reuse of one Skolem-function event name across several independent rules ((sk_go_out $x) in the Middle Row distribution rule and in both strength-0 "No lantern ..." rules) — nothing says whether Skolem function names must be distinct per rule, so overlapping domains would collide on one term at strengths 1.0 and 0.0
review.notes: The hard parts are right: the wind is Patient as an intransitive natural force but Agent as a transitive subject, go_out stays a whole phrasal symbol, (Yet sk_add_1) sits outside the denial, "before dawn" is TimeAtMost on a day-part constant, and the "No lantern" clauses take the strength-0 rule with its QuantifierPhrase companion. The three issues above are a dropped tense, one unstated identification, and one denial-boundary placement.

issues.reason: "were unprepared" is a past-tense copular, and the instruction set's surface-tense rule wraps every categorical atom such a clause yields, so the distributed conclusion must be (Past (Member $x unprepared)); the bare atom asserts a tenseless unprepared state the text restricts to that night.

Nothing in the text says the cold wind that blew off the sea is the north wind, so (Member sk_wind_1 north_wind) fails the Core-patterns "point at the words that put the atom there" test and asserts an identification the passage never states.

"Keepers on the Cliff Path" is a bare plural, i.e. indefinite, and the determiner test in Core patterns plus the worked "A cooper does not caulk the barrel" example ("indefinite subject — stays inside") place an indefinite subject's witness and typing inside the strength-0 (And …), not beside it.

gaps_confirmed: a solid-spelled name with the kind word fused into it ("the Northcove") — the type-atom licence is stated for a kind word sitting inside a multi-word name ("the Kestrel River" → river) and it is unstated whether a fused morpheme counts, which is why the parse typed sunken_cove but not northcove

Ordinal's scale slot when the ranked thing is itself an event-noun kind ("the first hard frost") — the stated fillers are the associated event or an explicit -est dimension, and an event-noun class in that slot is unillustrated

no stated convention keeping Skolem-function event names distinct per rule — (sk_go_out $x) is reused by the Middle Row distribution rule and both strength-0 "No lantern …" rules, so overlapping domains would land strength 1.0 and 0.0 on one term
new_gaps: a causal connective whose BOTH endpoints are denied clauses ("Keepers had not yet added …, because the season had not started") — the connective atom relates the two event witnesses and carries no polarity, so (Because sk_add_1 sk_start_1) and the seeded ReasonFor bridge read as a reason relation between two events that did not occur; a licensed form would have to carry the polarity of each endpoint

a day-of-year ordinal date ("On day 16 of Year 1") — the Time term (Day <n>) is the day-of-month term ("June 5, 2021" → (Day 5)) and there is no term for a day index counted within a year, so a fictional or ordinal-day calendar has no faithful carrier
adjudication.defect_summary: The unprepared clause's compliant form is the tense-wrapped distribution (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lanterns_1) (Past (Member $x unprepared))); "the north wind" must take a fresh first-mention witness, (Member sk_wind_2 north_wind) filling the Against slot, instead of being fused with sk_wind_1; and the keepers' (GroupOf sk_keepers_1 keeper) plus its (On sk_keepers_1 cliff_path) restrictor belong inside the strength-0 (And …) bundle.
adjudication.notes: One defect the reviewer missed: "add" is distributive, so the negated plural should emit both the group denial and a per-member rule at strength 0.0 ("A negated plural or group keeps both emissions"), as the parse itself did for the lanterns' go_out.
